segments.title: Name, address, date and recording setup
segments.summary: Allen confirms Babe's real name is Jewel Stovall, the address, the date (April 16, 1974) and tests the microphone.

segments.title: Why he is called Babe; birth in 1907
segments.summary: Family gave him the name Babe; he was born October 4, 1907, in Crystal Springs (Tylertown, Mississippi, per his record).

segments.title: Learning guitar; brother Tom and early parties
segments.summary: He was the only guitarist in the family besides his violin-playing brother Tom, and played at parties for little or no pay.

segments.title: Whiskey, food and bootleggers at country parties
segments.summary: Musicians were paid in whiskey; bootleggers sold beer and fried chicken at parties.

segments.title: Getting a guitar from his brother; two-finger picking and slapping
segments.summary: Started around age eight or nine on his brother's guitar, learned two-finger picking, and taught himself to slap the box.

segments.title: Tuning, picks and the twelve-string guitar
segments.summary: He tunes one way, uses thumb and finger, and played a twelve-string with three strings removed; also mentions Saints and old-time religion.

segments.title: Church of God in Christ and singing blues and religious songs
segments.summary: Raised in the sanctified church; he sings religious songs and blues and says the church does not object. Briefly mentions his wife and ten children.

segments.title: Guitarists around Tylertown and Jackson: Tommy Johnson, Bracey, McCoys
segments.summary: Questions about other guitar players in Mississippi, including Tommy Johnson, Ishman Bracey, the McCoy brothers, Big Joe Williams; he played with no one but Tom.

segments.title: Steel guitars, dobro and bottleneck
segments.summary: He never played electric guitar, prefers steel-bodied guitars, and has not used a fretless or bottleneck style.

segments.title: Work as a young man: cross ties, Franklin and Bogalusa
segments.summary: He cut cross ties and worked in Franklin, Louisiana, and did little music work in the country before moving to New Orleans; also where he learned songs.

segments.title: Coming to New Orleans, Preservation Hall and touring colleges
segments.summary: He came to New Orleans, played at Preservation Hall with his brother, and toured colleges in California, New York and elsewhere.

segments.title: His youngest child and his schooling
segments.summary: Chat with his thirteen-year-old daughter; he had little schooling and no music lessons.

segments.title: Playing Jackson Square and the Dream Castle
segments.summary: He has played Jackson Square for fifteen or sixteen years and played at the Dream Castle; mentions his stolen steel guitar and a gift guitar.

segments.title: Making records and Larry Borenstein
segments.summary: He made records, felt underpaid, and says Larry (Borenstein) got him to record; Sylvester Handy mentioned.

segments.title: Travels, piano players, dirty songs and the capo; reel change
segments.summary: He never went to Texas, Memphis or the Carolinas; questions about piano players, bawdy songs and capo, then a tape reel change.

segments.title: Playing with David Solero; the Jazz Festival
segments.summary: Asked about playing with David Solero, who has left town; he will play the Jazz Festival.

segments.chapter: Life in New Orleans and tunings
segments.title: Christmas and New Year's parties; why he moved to New Orleans
segments.summary: Country parties at holidays and little pay, which is why he came to the city to earn money.

segments.chapter: Life in New Orleans and tunings
segments.title: Alternate guitar tunings
segments.summary: He tunes many different ways without names for them and cannot read music.

segments.chapter: Life in New Orleans and tunings
segments.title: Moving to New Orleans in 1963; family; jazz festival and tours
segments.summary: He came to New Orleans in 1963; his brothers have died; he has played only the New Orleans jazz festival plus a college tour.

segments.chapter: Life in New Orleans and tunings
segments.title: Playing outdoors and in bars; Edro Stovall
segments.summary: He mostly plays outdoors; he talks about playing with Edro Stovall, a guitarist and relative who uses a flat pick.

segments.chapter: Life in New Orleans and tunings
segments.title: Setting up to demonstrate tunings
segments.summary: The interviewers ask him to demonstrate tunings for a teacher; discussion of his new guitar and naming a song.

segments.chapter: Life in New Orleans and tunings
segments.title: Songs played in altered tunings
segments.summary: He plays and sings songs including old-time religion and a gospel number; ASR text is largely garbled.

segments.chapter: Life in New Orleans and tunings
segments.title: Other street guitarists and closing
segments.summary: He says he is the only street guitarist; the interviewers thank and pay him and end the session.
